name: OSEL Devices Limited

sections.title: Executive verdict
sections.text:
Fast growth, but not yet a reliable cash compounder. OSEL has built three operating lines: hearing aids, LED displays and licensed Philips phones. FY26 standalone sales grew 56.95% to ₹292.67 crore and PAT to ₹29.25 crore. This is not merely acquired growth: SFL clinic revenue was not included in FY26. Yet cumulative FY23–26 operating cash was−₹86.94 crore against ₹67.01 crore profit, even before capex. Receivables, supplier advances and inventory absorb the earnings.
The important distinction is between corrected and unresolved problems. Management acknowledged the earlier borrowing-in-CFO mistake, and the FY26 comparative now correctly moves ₹30.43 crore to financing. The latest full audit nevertheless contains incomplete warranty evidence, gaps in audit trails and an inability to reconcile bank inventory quantities directly to the consolidated inventory ledger. The main and IFC opinions are unmodified; this is not a fraud finding.
BQS 4.6 (raw 4.56), GQS 5.0 (raw 5.95, capped at 5 for persistent poor cash realization), IAS NS. G2 and G3 are Hold — unresolved. Exclude from investable rankings. This is a research hold, not a personalized sell instruction or a claim that default has occurred. The decision-changing evidence is a reconciled cash/commitment bridge, credible warranty accounting and a clear SFL ownership/consolidation statement.

sections.title: Research header, gates and data confidence
sections.text:
Deep research; framework v 3.0; information cutoff 20 October 2026, India exchange calendar; market reference 19 October 2026 official closing ₹346.45, not the later rolling webpage. Horizon 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031,1826 days/365.25. Equity hurdle 15% nominal annualized before investor taxes;12%/18% sensitivity. Illustrative liquidity position ₹500,000, not an allocation recommendation.
Issuer: OSEL Devices Limited; NSE Emerge, symbol OSELDEVICE, ISIN INE0RMF01018; formerly Innovative Infratech Solutions and subsequently OSEL Devices Private Limited. CIN L72200DL2006PLC152027. Indian Accounting Standards in the colloquial sense should not be confused with Ind AS: filings use Indian GAAP Accounting Standards and expressly cite the SME exemption from Ind AS. Figures are ₹crore unless specified.
Consolidated results are inspected in full, but the forecast isolates the 100%-owned listed-parent operating business. Group ownership/consideration and parent-attributable earnings are not sufficiently reconciled to forecast SFL as if its earnings belonged wholly to shareholders. No acquired profit is invented, no minority claim is subtracted twice, and no ordinary price target is offered. This limitation affects financial reliability and investment scoring, not the verified issuer identity.
G1 Conditional; G2 Hold — unresolved; G3 Hold — unresolved; G4 Conditional. Source confidence is high for quoted primary figures and official market rows, medium for economic interpretation and low for current unreported commitments/forecast financeability. ND means unavailable, NM not meaningful, NA not applicable and NS not scoreable, never an imputed neutral number.

sections.title: Scorecard and calculation audit
sections.text:
All thirteen factor audits below contain supporting evidence, contrary evidence, confidence and score-change triggers. Governance is GOV; GQS means Growth Quality. P means Price-implied expectations, not promoter quality. The stated weights are unaltered and never redistributed around missing factors. Decimal arithmetic and ROUND_HALF_UP one-decimal display are used; IAS takes unrounded final BQS once.
Raw BQS 4.56 is complete. Raw GQS 5.95 is capped at 5.00 because persistent poor cash realization triggers the framework ceiling; strong reported growth does not override it. IAS has 55% coverage: known contribution 2.54 and missing-factor range 2.99–7.04, not a point estimate or a ranking. R and P are NS because only hypothetical recapitalization returns are financeable in the illustrated model. No favorable score is manufactured from a counterfactual rescue.
The numerical quality scores are diagnostic judgments, not statistically validated predictions. G2/G3 prevent inclusion in investable rankings even though most operating factors are scoreable. CAP4 is supported by an explicit multi-year incremental bridge and counter-sensitivities; lack of private project cohorts alone is not used to force NS. D3 reflects quantified downside rather than an invented default.

sections.title: Business overview and economic engine
sections.text:
LED displays are designed, assembled, integrated and installed for commercial/institutional customers. Hearing aids combine device manufacturing and qualification with a nascent direct clinical channel. Philips feature phones and smart phones use licensed branding and distribution; management described outsourced job work for mobile manufacturing. These are different economics, not one homogeneous technology platform.
FY26 management mix is approximately 42% hearing,41% LED and 17% mobile, equivalent to ₹122.92/₹119.99/₹49.75 crore on reported sales. This is not an audited segment profit table. Revenue notes separately show ₹262.85 crore domestic goods,₹22.47 crore exports and ₹7.35 crore services. Services are only about 2.51% of sales and cannot all be assumed recurring Saa S. Claims about large future monthly software subscriptions remain forecasts; current ARR, churn and cohort retention are ND.
The cash engine is purchases/inventory, sales on credit and substantial supplier advances. FY26 inventory ₹57.96 crore and supplier advances ₹52.89 crore together exceed ₹110 crore before receivables ₹107.24 crore. Core profitability is real in reported accounts, but its financing cycle is more important than the technology narrative. Imports were ₹97.61 crore of purchasing inputs; July Colorlight localization still depends on external designs and components.
SFL remains a multi-brand clinical network, not a captive channel guaranteed to sell only OSEL devices. July 1 describes 41 operational centres after four partner additions; number of centres does not establish average revenue, profit, patient retention, or clinic ownership. JNPA is a development opportunity with deposits and an LOI, not an operating cash asset.

sections.title: Moat and industry position
sections.text:
The strongest moat argument is qualification plus local service capability: regulated-device manufacturing, a domestic display integration footprint, licensed brand distribution and a clinical channel can reduce a buyer’s execution burden. The counterargument is stronger than a generic “Make in India” label: critical controller technology and kits come from Colorlight; Philips is licensed rather than owned IP; clinics intentionally sell competing brands; advanced hearing features still require product development.
Historical concentration is severe: FY24 top five customers accounted for 81.31% and top ten 90.76%, with no long-term customer contracts stated in the prospectus. These are historical, not assumed FY26 shares. Management later described a major bank software agreement, which is useful counterevidence but not enough to infer company-wide recurring revenue. Pricing power, renewal cohorts and current customer concentration are ND.
Relevant comparators are Sonova in hearing devices/clinical retail, Barco in visualization and Dixon in electronics/mobile manufacturing. Sonova’s disclosed organic growth and strong segment margin demonstrate the value of IP and distribution; Barco’s cashflow demonstrates that display engineering can create cash; Dixon illustrates very different large-scale EMS economics. None is a directly comparable valuation multiple. Geography, scale, brand ownership, products, accounting and capital intensity differ. No same-date peer P/E is fabricated.
MOAT4 recognizes genuine operating capabilities without equating registration, awards, licensing or broad TAM with pricing power. An FDA facility registration is not an FDA product approval or evidence of superiority. The critical upgrade is demonstrated profitable retention and distinctive product economics, not another certification headline.

sections.title: Revenue growth and scale
sections.text:
The full annual series below covers FY22–26. Revenue rose ₹65.25→₹81.89→₹132.23→₹186.47→₹292.67 crore. The genuine three-year FY23–26 CAGR is 52.89%; the four-year endpoint CAGR is 45.53%. Five observations are four elapsed years, not a five-year CAGR. Verified FY21/FY16 full comparable endpoints are absent, so five/ten-year CAGRs remain ND rather than extrapolated.
FY26’s ₹106.20 crore revenue increment includes approximately ₹49.75 crore new mobile sales, about 46.85% of the increase if the reported 17% mix is used. This is internally developed new-product growth, not same-product organic growth. Legacy hearing/LED combined would be roughly ₹242.91 crore, approximately 30.27% above FY25, but this is a mix-based approximation, not an audited segment bridge. Exact volume, ASP, market share and same customer growth are ND.
SFL has no included FY26 revenue according to management, consistent with identical standalone/group sales. Its expected ₹26–27 crore future contribution is acquired growth and must be shown separately when consolidated. Export revenue expanded sharply from a negligible comparison base; it does not yet establish repeatable export demand or qualification-led pricing power.
REV8 reflects the ≥30% growth band but the medium confidence ceiling prevents 9–10. Historical COVID/rebound and recent product entry are explained rather than mechanically disqualifying a small company. Growth durability depends on profitable collections and available capital, not merely the arithmetic continuation of 53% CAGR.

sections.title: Growth quality and reinvestment runway
sections.text:
The incremental capital bridge uses normalized operating NOPAT at a disclosed 30% tax rate and financing-stock capital, equity plus interest bearing debt less reported cash. FY22→25, before SFL, adds ₹137.83 crore capital and ₹19.97 crore NOPAT, a 14.49% incremental proxy. FY23→26 adds ₹254.71 crore capital for ₹30.85 crore NOPAT,12.11%. FY25→26 is 10.27%. Excluding collateral financial assets changes the latest incremental proxy to 15.99%, a meaningful counter-sensitivity rather than evidence that funds are freely available.
These are not marginalproject IRRs. Cash classification, collateral balances, equity timing, mobile mix, property/capex and acquisition advances affect the denominator. A12–15% nominal capital cost range is an analyst scenario, not the 15% equity hurdle mislabeled WACC. The observations do not show a robust positive economic spread across plausible definitions. CAP4 therefore reflects a measured, uncertain return on deployed capital, not a claim of proven capital destruction.
Past physical capacity in the prospectus was 400,000 hearing aid units and 15,000 sqft LED annually; FY24 utilization 42.48%/47.50%. Those old figures cannot authenticate FY26 capacity or support a five-year bull volume forecast. Updated line capacity, yields, utilization, product mix and expansion milestones are ND. A much larger sales base may require new facilities, outsourced supply or different product mix.
The operating model explicitly funds incremental working capital, maintenance/growth capex, warranty costs, tax and debt service. JNPA capex and any remaining SFL consideration are two-way sensitivities, not invented committed numbers. Persistent weak cash triggers GQS ceiling 5. It is possible to grow revenue and reported profit while increasing financial risk and diluting per-share value; this is the central issue here.

sections.title: Management, governance and execution
sections.text:
Promoters held 64.84% at September 30,11,537,890 shares, with no share pledge reported. This must not be confused with the 65.2% diluted percentage or with corporate assets, which are pledged to lenders. Related party Guardian purchases ₹44.32 crore and payable ₹7.63 crore are material. Disclosed relationships and approvals do not alone establish unfair pricing; independent procurement benchmarking and continuing approval controls are needed.
The governance record is mixed, not a one-sided allegation. The earlier CFO classification was acknowledged and corrected; May 31 EPS typo was corrected; actual IFC and main audit opinions are unmodified; no reported lender default, willful default, fraud noticed or statutory auditor resignation was found. Against that, recurring reporting errors, warranty documentation, audit trail gaps and subsidiary scope inconsistencies make high confidence unwarranted.
The January CEO appointment broadens operational leadership. August CFO departure was disclosed with a personal reason; no financial misconduct is inferred and a replacement was not authenticated by cutoff. Execution has delivered product launches and higher exports, but an expanding portfolio, uncos ted park and clinic integration create demands beyond the old OEM business.
Capital allocation is assessed per-share: FY26 PAT grew 45.84% but reported basic EPS 19.92%, with preferential equity, warrants and ESOPs expanding claims. There are 160,000 actual granted options at ₹10, not 800,000 current issued shares. The remaining plan pool and October 170,000 warrant proposal are separate future branches. Promoter dividend waiver lowers company cash use but does not repair operating cash conversion.

sections.title: Financial forensics and accounting quality
sections.text:
The primary annual statement ledger, ageing rows, capital bridges and classification reconciliations are embedded below. Core FY26 operating EBITDA is ₹53.357 crore after removing ₹1.9037 crore other income. The annual headline ₹55.2607 crore includes other income; presentation group EBITDA ₹53.3279 crore also differs by group costs. These are explained definition/scope differences, not an unexplained profit surplus.
FY25 corrected CFO is−₹68.6529 crore versus original−₹38.2236 crore, exactly ₹30.4293 crore short-term borrowing reclassified to financing. The ₹19.1797→₹8.7475 crore comparative cash change matches ₹10.4322 crore investing reclassification. It is not treated as missing money. FY24 prospectus CFO ₹12.2045 crore differs from the later annual comparative even after removing borrowings; retain both presentations rather than silently splicing. FY24 PAT ₹13.0521 crore prospectus vs ₹12.6841 crore later comparison also has ₹0.368 crore prior tax difference.
The strongest unresolved issues are specific: warranty provision lacks supporting documentation; audit trail was inactive in periods; bank itemized stock could not be directly reconciled to consolidated quantities. CARO’s “10% or more” wording is not a disclosed stock loss amount. Main audit and actual IFC annexures are unmodified, which is relevant counterevidence, not a substitute for reading the exceptions. Tax notes and generic no-litigation language must be read together: actual GST dispute ₹9.982 crore with ₹3.1831 crore paid under protest, other matters and overdue statutory ₹0.209 crore require individual status, not indiscriminate summing.
SFL requires a documented closing/consideration/consolidation and ownership bridge. Healthcare is 71.14% owned in notes versus 100% in AOC 1; its 90.69% SFL stake implies 64.516866% effective ownership if both notes apply. ₹30 crore SPA and ₹16.25 crore book investment are not sufficient to prove ₹13.75 crore unpaid cash. ₹18.1578 crore“subsidiary reserve”financing could represent new minority subscriptions; it is not automatically noncash or fabricated. Current group owner PAT is ND. These gaps reinforce G2 Hold while stopping short of an accounting fraud allegation.

sections.title: Valuation, funding and price-implied expectations
sections.text:
Official price ₹346.45 times 17,794,600 shares gives ₹616.493917 crore market cap. Current-share base P/E on parent FY26 PAT is 21.08 x, not price divided by an unadjusted historical EPS. Cash-only enterprise value is ₹709.13 crore/13.29 x operating EBITDA. Netting all pledged funds/FD gives ₹650.50 crore/12.19 x, an asset-value cross-check rather than spendable liquidity. These mix October price with March balance and are not certified current net debt.
The dated core model starts March 31, with monthly points plus actual April 23₹2.55 crore equity receipt and known ₹0.6256772 crore dividend use. It reserves ₹1 crore minimum cash, tests 0/1/3, separately settle sold tax/statutory items, maintains revolving debt under an explicit renewal assumption and never counts optional warrants as received money. Growth 5/20/30%, EBITDA 12/18/19.5% before warranty, working capital 68/60/52% of run-rate sales and capex 2/3.5/4.5% are analyst bear/base/bull assumptions. No operating property is valued twice.
All three default paths breach cash floor, including pre-entry in this assumed trajectory. Funding gaps are ₹31.53/₹107.75/₹188.19 crore before unknown park/SFL incremental uses. This is not observed historical distress: actual post-March cash/obligations are unreported, and selected tax/timing assumptions matter. Matched collateral release, lower old tax and new facility stress explicitly test alternatives; rating limits are not free cash. Ordinary IRRs and entry prices remain NS regardless of a lower stock price.
A separately labeled counterfactual raises whole equity shares on March 31,2026, before any modeled trough, at 25% discount to ₹346.45 with 2% fees. It pre-funds every interval and includes extra eligible dividend shares. This is not an available offer. Funded bear/base/bull IRRs are-19.03%/11.66%/28.45%; ownership dilution differs from share count expansion. Terminal cash reserve is retained; collateral recoveries have 5%/10% haircuts; old gratuity is reserved; granted ESOPs dilute without assumed funding credit. SFL and advances receive no incremental terminal value because their cashflows are unreconciled, not because their true value is zero.
Reverse expectation and 5 x/10 x solvers first find a finite funded bracket, then verify crossing/residual. They allow funding/dilution to change with growth; no endpoint masquerades as a solution. These conditional outputs are useful requirements, not a current P score or promised return.

sections.title: Bear case and permanent-loss pathways
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is that OSEL’s apparent profitable growth requires a permanently larger receivable/supplier advance/inventory base while pricing power is limited. Warranty costs, credit losses or failed advances could then erode already thin free cash. Even without a lender default today, repeated capital raises can transfer future upside to new capital and leave existing holders with weak per-share returns.
A linked stress combines slower 5% growth,12% EBITDA before 2% warranty,68% working capital and 7 x exit multiple. The counterfactual funded bear case suffers a large annualized loss despite continuing operation. This is more informative than only haircutting the P/E. Separate branches test GST cash calls, old tax credits, bank availability, matched collateral release, park budgets and SFL consideration. Additional debt is not treated as free equity and negative cash is never silently funded.
The positive counter case is meaningful: no reported current lender default; investment grade BBB-level rationales; substantial collateral; reported operating profit; real April warrant cash; corrected historical CFO presentation. Full Infomerics January 29 assessed liquidity as adequate, citing 67% average utilization through October 2025 and September 2025 cash ₹31.84 crore, free FD ₹11 crore and accessible MF ₹30 crore. These are dated counterevidence, not March 2026 availability: the September cash-flow caption included fixed deposits and later notes specifically pledge the funds. CRISIL/Infomerics working capital metrics use different scopes, so no false like-for-like ratio comparison is made. These facts prevent a “Fail — evidenced” finding solely from a forecast gap. The decisive risk is not inevitable insolvency but whether growth and commitments can be funded without unfavorable recapitalization or impaired asset realization.
Thesis-break variables are collections/advances and funded commitments, not simply reported revenue growth. A full receivable ageing and supplier advance closeout, lender limits/covenant headroom, warranty assessment and SFL closing statement would change the decision more than another order announcement.

sections.title: 5x and 10x feasibility
sections.text:
Small market capitalization alone does not establish multibagger potential. A 5 x or 10 x share price requires growth in value per existing claim, after funding new capital, debt, reserves, warrant/option dilution and minority attribution. The embedded counterfactual solvers target terminal share price multiples of ₹346.45, not merely total company market cap. The known ₹1 dividend is separately included in IRR, not mislabeled 5 x capital gain.
The solver uses the base 10 x after-warranty EBITDA exit multiple and base capital intensity, allowing required recapitalization share count to increase with growth. It does not hold shares constant while funding working capital with nothing. Each output includes required annual growth, terminal revenue/EBITDA, equity raised, final shares and residual; a missing crossing stays NS. Neither the 5 x nor the 10 x target has a funded finite crossing in the tested 0–200% annual-growth range. No growth solution is reported. This is a limitation of these base margin, capital-intensity and financing assumptions, not proof that those outcomes are impossible under every different business model. The required capacity, product mix, market share and funding are not established by present disclosures.
For context, the five-year compound growth ofa 5 x/10 x investment would be about 38%/58% annually before tax, far above ordinary hurdles. OSEL’s recent 52.9% three-year sales CAGR does not guarantee a similar per share value CAGR. Dependence on imported technology, license continuity, customer concentration and cash conversion becomes more important with scale. Classification: speculative upside exists, but not a demonstrated 5 x/10 x underwritten compounder.

sections.title: Monitoring dashboard
sections.text:
At each results release: reconcile operating cash excluding financing, cumulative CFO/PAT, receivables>6 months, inventories and supplier advances. Upgrade evidence would include two years of positive CFO and cumulative CFO/PAT above 0.8 without factoring/debt masked as operating cash. Investigate fresh ageing, write-offs, related party balances and rebased comparatives.
Before any investment reassessment: obtain updated bank fund-based limits, utilization, covenant terms/renewals, pledged fund/FD release conditions and the complete cash/commitment calendar. Reconcile old tax credits and settlements; authenticate SFL consideration paid/payable, control/consolidation date, owners PAT and outside equity subscriptions; obtain JNPA approved capex, contracts and milestones. A rating amount is not enough.
Control checkpoints: next auditor report and full CARO/IFC/audit trail annexures, quantified warranty provision methodology, inventory quantity/bank returns, finance leadership replacement and related procurement benchmarking. Commercial checkpoints: audited segment profit/cash, current concentration, hearing clinic unit metrics, mobile ASP/returns, license conditions and recurring software ARR/churn.
Capital dates: promoter warrants expire around late December 2026 subject original terms; employee options vest May 29,2027; October new warrants require approval/allotment before cash can be counted. Dividend record Oct 24,2026 and assumed payment Nov 16 must be updated to actual receipt. Recheck lot, active exchange series, surveillance and live order depth before execution; turnover history is not a standing execution assurance.

sections.title: Classification and conditional action
sections.text:
Classification: fast reported growth with weak cash realization and unresolved financial/funding reliability. Research hold; not an investable ranked recommendation. BQS 4.56, GQS 5.00 after ceiling, IAS NS. No high-quality compounder designation or attractive-entry label is supported while G2/G3 remain Hold. A lower market price alone does not repair issuer funding or warranty/scope accounting.
A conditional upgrade requires reliable owners financials and a funded dated operating plan, not necessarily private daily bank statements. Public recent cash, confirmed facilities, binding commitment coverage and collected receivables can be sufficient. If those resolve favorably, rebuild R/P/IAS from ordinary cashflows and verified shares; do not reuse counterfactual rescue prices as purchase levels.
For an existing holder, this report does not infer portfolio allocation, tax position or liquidity needs. The ₹5 lakh reference is only an implementation test. Any action must consider concentration and ability to exit during one-sided SME trading. The analysis is informational, not personalized financial advice, and model outcomes are conditional rather than predictions.

sections.title: Sources, assumptions and open questions
sections.text:
Primary sources include the complete FY26/FY25 annual reports, NSE-hosted IPO prospectus, corrected May 31 results/ESOP grant, June 2 presentation/transcript, dated capital/allotment, SFL SPA, JNPA announcement, September ownership, October dividend/warrant outcome, rating rationales and 60 official bhavcopies plus dated security master. Original documents were inspected; the ledger records URLs, original payload hashes where available and precise locators. Company forecasts are labeled as claims, not verified outcomes.
The company website’s small blank“prospectus.pdf” was rejected and replaced with the full NSE prospectus. The October 21 EGM notice is after cutoff and is not used. Source-safe extracts reproduce calculations but cannot re-authenticate original filings by themselves. No original PDF/OCR, individual tax identifiers, shareholder personal data or transfer credentials belong in the deliverable.
Open questions are material: SFL closing/cash consideration and owner attribution; Healthcare AOC 1 contradictions; composition of subsidiary reserve financing; warranty exposure; bank inventory quantity reconciliation; updated loan headroom/renewal terms; tax credits/settlement status; supplier advance recovery; current product/customer profitability; JNPA committed budget; future license economics. Missing information is explicit, not replaced with neutral scores or notional cash.
The complete historical, model, annual forecast, dated cash, sensitivity, reverse expectation and scoring rows are embedded in the canonical record and readable appendices. All forecast assumptions are separated from observed facts. The backups contain rebuild able safe builders/inputs; reconstruction checks authenticate arithmetic and artifact integrity, not an investment outcome.

evidence.claim: Standalone revenue rose from ₹81.8868 cr FY23 to ₹292.6681 cr FY26,52.8928% CAGR; five/ten-year comparable endpoints unavailable.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: New mobile product launch is organic but unseasoned. Future SFL revenue is acquired, not organic.

evidence.claim: FY26 approximate revenue mix 42% hearing aids,41% LED,17% mobile; FY25 credit rationale gives 54% hearing/46% LED.

evidence.claim: FY24 top 10 customers 90.76%, top 5 81.31%; prospectus states no long-term customer contracts.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: June 2 says a major bank Saa S agreement exists; no current concentration/order book ageing supplied. Historical concentration not assumed unchanged.

evidence.claim: FY26 domestic goods ₹262.8488 cr, exports ₹22.4677 cr, services ₹7.3516 cr; prior exports ₹0.0018 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Export jump is a small-base expansion, not established recurring overseas franchise.

evidence.claim: Core capabilities include hearing-device qualifications, display integration and licensed Philips distribution. July 16 Colorlight supplies designs, BOM and CKD/SKD components; OSEL assembles/tests/markets.

evidence.claim: FY23–26 comparable-basis standalone cumulative CFO−₹86.9371 cr vs PAT ₹67.0098 cr, CFO/PAT−1.2974 x.

evidence.claim: FY25 CFO was corrected from−₹38.2236 cr to−₹68.6529 cr by moving ₹30.4293 cr short-term borrowing to financing. Management explicitly acknowledged error June 2.

summary:
Fast growth, but not yet a reliable cash compounder. OSEL has built three operating lines: hearing aids, LED displays and licensed Philips phones. FY26 standalone sales grew 56.95% to ₹292.67 crore and PAT to ₹29.25 crore. This is not merely acquired growth: SFL clinic revenue was not included in FY26. Yet cumulative FY23–26 operating cash was−₹86.94 crore against ₹67.01 crore profit, even before capex. Receivables, supplier advances and inventory absorb the earnings.
The important distinction is between corrected and unresolved problems. Management acknowledged the earlier borrowing-in-CFO mistake, and the FY26 comparative now correctly moves ₹30.43 crore to financing. The latest full audit nevertheless contains incomplete warranty evidence, gaps in audit trails and an inability to reconcile bank inventory quantities directly to the consolidated inventory ledger. The main and IFC opinions are unmodified; this is not a fraud finding.
BQS 4.6 (raw 4.56), GQS 5.0 (raw 5.95, capped at 5 for persistent poor cash realization), IAS NS. G2 and G3 are Hold — unresolved. Exclude from investable rankings. This is a research hold, not a personalized sell instruction or a claim that default has occurred. The decision-changing evidence is a reconciled cash/commitment bridge, credible warranty accounting and a clear SFL ownership/consolidation statement.
